issues_found.issue: Dodge i-frames do not exist in real PvP. Hit resolution is shooter-authoritative -- _onProjectileHit bails with 'Someone else's shot: we only draw it, the owner reports it' and only the owner sends {type:'hit'}. The new `hittable` filter removes the LOCAL player from the target set in the LOCAL client only. A remote human shooting you resolves the hit in THEIR client, which has no knowledge of your `player.iframes`, so their shot lands anyway. The i-frames therefore only work against bots and your own local sim -- exactly the case that matters least. Worse, the HUD pip flashes 'active' and the player will believe they dodged, so the feature actively teaches a lie in 8-player matches.
issues_found.suggestion: Replicate the dodge over the network. Cheapest fix: broadcast a lightweight `{type:'ev', dodge:true}` (or add an `iframes`/`inv` flag to the existing input/state tick in server/room.js) so remote clients can filter a dodging player out of their own `parts` target list before resolving. Alternative: keep it shooter-authoritative but let the victim veto -- on receiving a 'hit', the target's client rejects it if it was inside its i-frame window, and the server applies damage only on victim ack. Until one of these ships, either scope the dodge as a pure mobility burst (drop the i-frames and the glow) or label it clearly as bot-only.

issues_found.issue: dodge() gates on canMove/frozen/crouching/swimming but NOT on `this.grounded`. A mid-air double-tap grants a 14 m/s horizontal air-dash that overrides the velocity cap (player.js:260-265 hard-sets vel.x/vel.z while dodgeTime > 0), bypassing the deliberately low air ACCEL of 14 and air FRICTION of 0.6. Jump + dodge chains give noticeably longer gap-crossing than the movement tuning intends -- on a tiny hand-made planet that is a map-skip risk, and it makes the roll a traversal tool rather than the committed combat decision the code comment claims.
issues_found.suggestion: Either add `if (!this.grounded) return false;` to dodge(), or deliberately keep the air-dash but give it its own reduced speed (~10) and no i-frames. Decide which -- right now it is an accident, not a choice.

issues_found.issue: Inconsistent i-frame coverage across weapon families. The `hittable` filter is applied to this.projectiles.update() and _driveBots(), but the local melee/soak path at line 988 sends {type:'hit', damage: stats.soak} through a separate code path that never consults iframes. So the dodge dodges projectiles but not melee. Given the lead's explicit BOTH decision (sabers and projectiles both first-class), a defensive verb that only counters one family breaks the rock-paper-scissors intent before it is even built.
issues_found.suggestion: Route all damage application through one helper (e.g. _tryHit(target, damage)) that checks target invulnerability once, so melee and projectiles share the same i-frame rule.

issues_found.issue: On entering water the code does `if (inWater && this.dodgeTime > 0) this.dodgeTime = 0;` but leaves `this.iframes` and `this.dodgeCooldown` running. A player who rolls into the sea keeps up to 0.12s of invulnerability while swimming, with the burst already cancelled -- a small free-invuln edge case, and the HUD pip briefly shows 'active' with no roll happening.

The filtered `hittable` list is also passed to _driveBots(). For 0.12s the local player vanishes from the bots' world, not just from their hit resolution -- bots may drop or re-pick targets mid-burst rather than simply missing. The intent (per the comment) was 'neither projectiles nor bot aim can resolve on them', but this couples aiming and target acquisition.
issues_found.suggestion: Pass the full `parts` to _driveBots for targeting and apply the i-frame filter only at the moment of hit resolution.
